newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases as cash levels rise.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases as cash levels rise.

text.p: German call money rates eased to 2.975/3.00 percent on Monday from 3.00/3.05 percent on Friday as the market was furnished with adequate liquidity, dealers said.
Rates were unlikely to change during the day and dealers predicted an uneventful trading session. "With these liquidity levels, not much can happen," one dealer said.

Bank holdings at the Bundesbank jumped to 39.3 billion marks on Friday from 36.9 billion marks on Thursday. Meanwhile the daily average for the month through Sunday rose to 38.5 billion marks from 38.3 billion.

Borrowing from the Lombard facility was little changed at about 100 million marks last Friday. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA was set at 3.04300 percent on Monday, compared with 3.04633 percent on Friday.
